To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) embodiment is the way in which our bodies are part of our understanding of the world and the world's understanding of us, 2) the five themes of thinking through doing, perform-ance, visibility, risk and thick practice are central to understanding embodiment, and 3) these five themes can be used to inspire new interaction design approaches and evaluations that better inte-grate the physical and computational world.
the physical body is an active participant in the interaction process and that interaction design should take into account the physical body as an active participant in interaction.
embodiment plays a central role in understanding human experience in theworld, and that interaction design should consider embodiment in its approach to design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how bodies matter, and how we can better design to account for the ways in which our bodies are central to the experience of interacting with digital artifacts and environments.
understanding how people use their bodies to interact with the world, and how the physical world influences how people think about and use technology.
understanding and supporting embodied engagement with the world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the body matters in HCI, and it is important for us as designers to be able to understand the body and its role in the design process.
the body is the most complex and sophisticated machine ever built.
the body is not only a physical entity but also an important factor in human interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the body is a central part of the interaction design process, and it is important to consider the role of the body in the design of technology.
we are interested in the ways in which people's bodies are implicated in their interactions with technology, and how these interactions are shaped by the physical and social world.
our bodies are not just a vehicle for our mind but are a part of what it is to be a mind, and thus a part of what is involved in our experience of the world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the body is an integral and central part of interaction design.
interaction design is not just a matter of designing interfaces, but of designing for the embodied experiences that emerge in the interaction of people and technology.
interaction design is not only about the design of interactions, but also about the design of embodied engagement.
